newsitem.title: CHINA: China calls for end to Cold War ideology.
newsitem.headline: China calls for end to Cold War ideology.

text.p: China's Defence Minister Chi Haotian on Thursday called for an end to Cold War ideology ahead of a visit by U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher.

"Now that the Cold War is over, words such as 'containment' and 'isolation' should be changed to...'friendly cooperation'," the Xinhua news agency quoted Chi as telling visiting U.S. Senate minority leader Thomas Daschle.
Containment was a U.S. Cold War strategy to prevent the spread of communism from the former Soviet bloc.

China suspects the United States is trying to contain its development. Washington denies this, saying it is seeking to engage, not contain, China but senior U.S. officials have warned that a need to contain China could arise in the future.
Daschle, a South Dakota Democrat, also met state president and Communist Party boss Jiang Zemin, who said the U.S. Congress could play a major role in promoting Sino-U.S. relations, Xinhua said.
Jiang was quoted as saying improving Sino-U.S. ties was in the interest of both countries.

China and the United States have seen ties strained in recent years over Taiwan, human rights, trade, copyright violations, arms proliferation and Beijing's long-delayed bid to join the World Trade Organisation.
Beijing has said Christopher's November 19-21 visit was important and that the two giants had more interests in common than differences.
Christopher's last visit to China two years ago ended in bitter wrangling over human rights issues.
Minister Chi is expected to visit the United States before the end of the year.
